title: Sable Therapeutics - Incident Follow-up (Postmortem)
summary: Postmortem follow-up covering last week's high-latency incident affecting inference on private deployment. Discussed root cause (KV cache invalidation after autoscaler churn + misrouted fallback to larger model), mitigations (runbook updates, staging canary for autoscaling), planned reliability improvements (cache warming, rolling restarts, improved tracer metrics) and next steps (benchmarks, security doc share, prioritized action items).
action_items: Maya Patel: Share incident timeline + logs export with Sable (by 2026-06-19)
Daniel Kim: Implement cache-warm startup hook prototype and push to staging (by 2026-06-23)
Markus Holt: Run load benchmark with KV-cache-disabled and share results (by 2026-06-22)
Priya Rao: Update postmortem runbook with autoscaler thresholds and rollback steps (by 2026-06-21)
Aisha Khan: Confirm KMS rotation policy and provide required docs for audit (by 2026-06-25)
next_steps: Redwood to deliver scoped mitigation plan and timeline (Maya + Daniel)
Customer to run replicated load test in staging and share results
Schedule a 30-min technical follow-up with SREs on 2026-06-24
Redwood to circulate security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts
Agree on a 2-week pilot for cache-warming patch then review metrics
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-18 14:30 PDT | Duration: ~52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Lena (Sable VP Eng), Markus (Sable SRE), Aisha (Sable Security)

Summary: quick walk through of last Thursday's incident where Sable saw a sustained latency spike and increased error rate for model endpoints in their private deployment. Goal: align on root cause, short-term mitigations and longer-term reliability improvements.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to go through the postmortem quickly, make sure we're aligned on what happened and next steps. Lena, do you want to start with what you observed on your side?
[00:12] Lena: Yeah thanks. So timeline from our monitoring: at ~02:40 UTC on 6/12 we saw a jump in tail latency for several endpoints, error rate spiked to ~8% for about 18 minutes. Our dashboards showed a lot of 503s and timeouts from the Inference gateway. We also saw some AWS autoscaler churn around the same time.
[00:34] Markus: To add, we had node terminations in the GPU pool and some pods restarted. Because of the way our KV cache is configured, when instances came back they weren't warmed and first requests experienced long runtimes while the model reloaded kv caches.
[00:50] Daniel: Right, from Redwood's telemetry the request routing briefly fell back to a larger non-quantized model variant while the optimized worker was reinitializing. That added CPU/GPU overhead and increased token latency. There's also a small bug where the fallback policy wasn't honoring a hard timeout, so retries queued.
[01:12] Lena: We saw a cascading effect — slower responses caused client retries which increased load, which blocked the cache warm paths further.
[01:25] Maya: Ok that's helpful. so root cause we think is combination of (1) autoscaler churn producing cold workers with un-warmed KV cache, (2) fallback routing to heavier model variant during recovery, and (3) retry amplification on the client side. Any disagreement on that framing?
[01:40] Markus: No, that matches our traces. The trace IDs that timed out line up with worker cold starts.
[01:48] Aisha: From security perspective nothing data-loss-wise occurred, but we want audit logs and key access timeline to confirm no anomalous access during the restarts.
[02:00] Daniel: We'll pull the key access logs and include them in the timeline.

[02:10] Maya: Let's cover short-term mitigations that we've already pushed and what's left. Daniel?
[02:16] Daniel: Yesterday we merged a quick fix that enforces a hard timeout on fallback routing so requests don't pile into slower variants; we've also added a temporary sampling-based rate limiter at the gateway during pod churn windows. Those are in staging and we can push to prod once you give the go-ahead.
[02:36] Markus: That timeout looks good; we want to validate under 80% load in staging first.
[02:42] Daniel: Agreed. Next immediate action is a cache-warm startup hook — on warmup the worker will prepopulate hot key prefixes and hold a short warm-only traffic window to avoid serving cold requests. We're prototyping that now.
[02:58] Lena: What's the expected extra startup time for warming?
[03:02] Daniel: Depends on model and hot-set size; for your deployment we estimate 3–7s to populate common prefixes. That's better than the 20–30s cold-run penalty we saw last week.
[03:14] Maya: Good, and Priya — runbook?
[03:17] Priya: I've started a runbook draft. adding steps: detect autoscaler churn threshold, initiate temporary rate limiting, shift traffic to canary region if available, and rollback policy. Also adding communication templates for the on-call and account team.
[03:30] Lena: We also raised a question about autoscaler settings. our min nodes are low to save cost. Are there recommendations from Redwood about min pool sizes for steady production load?
[03:41] Daniel: Yes, we recommend setting a small buffer min (1–2 spare workers depending on QPS) to avoid cold starts during spikes. We can run simulations against your QPS traces to recommend exact numbers.

[03:56] Aisha: On the security/compliance side, we need the timeline, audit logs, and confirmation that KMS keys were not re-created or rotated during the incident. also would like the SOC2 artifact we discussed earlier.
[04:12] Maya: We'll share the SOC2 summary and KMS access logs. Daniel will pull the timeline.
[04:18] Daniel: I'll include trace fragments that show the routing decisions and the fallback events.

[04:22] Lena: Quick technical deep dive: can we avoid fallback to the heavier model entirely during recovery windows? It seems like a config gate might be better than runtime fallback.
[04:32] Daniel: We can add a configuration flag to disable model-variant fallback per-route. The tradeoff is that some requests will error instead of completing with degraded but acceptable output. We should align on per-route SLOs; for critical flows you might prefer guaranteed latency over degraded semantics.
[04:50] Markus: For our real-time chat endpoint we prefer timeouts over incorrect completions, so disabling fallback is acceptable. For nightly batch jobs maybe fallback is fine.

[05:05] Maya: Ok, action items recap coming. But one more question on observability: we noticed insufficient warm-cache metrics — we had no good signal of how many keys were loaded. Can we add finer-grained metrics?
[05:18] Daniel: Yes, we'll add counters: cache_warm_hits, cache_warm_misses, warm_duration_seconds histogram and an alert when warm_misses exceed threshold. We'll also tag by node and model variant.
[05:30] Lena: that will help a lot.

[05:35] Priya: On the process side, propose a 2-week pilot for the cache-warm hook in staging + a canary rollout to a small percentage of prod traffic with increased telemetry.
[05:45] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Any blockers for the pilot?
[05:48] Markus: Need a checklist on the rollback steps and a clear load test window.
[05:53] Priya: I'll write the rollback checklist and coordinate the load test dates.

[06:00] Aisha: For audit trail, we'll need signed confirmation that access to customer keys did not change during the incident and a copy of the flow that reads the KMS keys.
[06:10] Daniel: We'll extract that and include it in the packet.

[06:15] Maya: Alright let's do a quick readout of the timeline and owners: Redwood will deliver logs+timeline (Maya/Daniel), run prototype warm-up hooks (Daniel), push runbook edits (Priya), Sable to run staging load tests and confirm min pool sizing (Markus/Lena). Security artifacts requested (Aisha).
[06:35] Lena: that's accurate. We appreciate the quick response.

[06:40] Maya: Anything else?

[06:42] Markus: Just one ask — can Redwood provide a checklist of configuration knobs (autoscaler min, fallback switch, warm window) and recommended defaults for common QPS ranges?
[06:53] Daniel: Yes we'll produce that as part of the mitigation plan.

[06:58] Maya: Great. we'll share next steps and schedule the follow-up 30-min SRE call for 2026-06-24. thanks everyone.
[07:07] End of recording.

Notes: Transcription contains typical ASR errors in proper nouns and punctuation; speaker turns are approximate. The recorded timeline numbers align with the 52-minute meeting duration.
